name: iPhone Duo
criticsTake: Critics say Apple's first foldable is the best-built foldable yet. The titanium hinge and the matte nano-texture display that hides the crease draw wide praise, and PCMag calls its battery life class-leading. It is also heavy at 254 g and starts at $1,999, it has no Face ID or telephoto camera, and many apps are not optimized yet, so The Verge, Wired and CNN suggest waiting.
loved: Polished titanium build and smooth hinge
Matte nano-texture inner display that hides the crease
gripes: No telephoto camera and no Face ID
Many third-party apps not optimized yet

specs.label: Inner display
specs.value: 7.6-inch OLED, matte nano-texture, ProMotion up to 120Hz

specs.label: Unlock
specs.value: Touch ID in the side button (no Face ID)

specs.label: Battery
specs.value: Up to 24 hours typical use; 50% in about 20 minutes

name: iPhone 18 Pro
criticsTake: Critics call the iPhone 18 Pro an excellent but iterative upgrade. The A20 Pro chip, longer battery life and a variable-aperture main camera with manual controls earn near-universal praise, while the unchanged design, extra weight and $100 price increase leave most reviewers telling iPhone 17 Pro owners to wait.
loved: A20 Pro performance, with better cooling than the 17 Pro
Variable-aperture main camera and new manual controls
gripes: Little visible change from the iPhone 17 Pro

specs.label: Display
specs.value: 6.3-inch OLED, ProMotion up to 120Hz, 3000 nits outdoor peak

specs.label: Rear cameras
specs.value: 48MP main with variable aperture (f/1.48 to f/4.0), 48MP ultra wide, 48MP 4x telephoto

specs.label: Battery
specs.value: Up to 36 hours video playback; 50% in about 15 minutes

name: Galaxy Z Fold 8
criticsTake: Critics love the Galaxy Z Fold 8's new wider, passport-shaped design, which makes it easy to use shut and great for video and games when open. Bright displays with a barely visible crease and solid battery life round out the praise. Nearly every review knocks the missing telephoto camera, and many flag the price, the IP48 rating and apps that don't yet fit the new screen shape.
loved: Wider passport design that is comfortable folded and great for video unfolded
Bright 120Hz displays with a much less visible crease
gripes: Still only IP48 dust and water resistance
Some apps don't scale to the new aspect ratio
Runs warm and throttles under sustained load
